scopeDecisions.recommendation: Use behavioral conditions rather than a raw API-method denominator; each declared transaction surface must map to exactly one condition.
Keep query execution inside a transaction here, following the FS-QUERY-INDEX Q4d decision; ordinary query semantics stay with FS-QUERY-INDEX.
Count the atomic visibility of all writes in one transaction commit on native Listen here; SDK callback delivery belongs to FS-LISTEN-SDK.
scopeDecisions.decision: The atomic visibility of a transaction commit on native Listen is assigned to FS-TRANSACTION; SDK callback shape is assigned to FS-LISTEN-SDK.

scopeDecisions.recommendation: Count the named idle and total transaction time limits in their expiry conditions; transaction size belongs to FS-DATA-WRITE.
scopeDecisions.decision: Idle and total time limits are assigned to their transaction expiry conditions; transaction size is assigned to FS-DATA-WRITE.

scopeDecisions.recommendation: Use the sandbox conformance-harness process with clean-context corpus/runner review, two recordings and one JSONL ledger line per run. The old single-run O8 manifest is preparation material only; do not import O7/O8 Gate or reservation tooling. A fresh owner go-ahead remains necessary under the current production-send hold.
Retain historical fireemu-35fe6 recordings as immutable reference only; require sandbox evidence or an explicit owner decision before calling any historical-only condition VERIFIED.
Keep SDK-driven retry distinct from backend retry-token semantics. Do not exclude it on the strength of REST or gRPC observations.
scopeDecisions.decision: Keep SDK retry separate from backend retry-token behavior.
This closure covers PESSIMISTIC mode only; OPTIMISTIC modes remain in a follow-up issue and are not known-difference exclusions.

conditions.note: Two sandbox recordings and both fireemu profiles agreed for this REST subset when it was recorded; that agreement was measured at strict's old 10 s idle allowance, with 90 s of local idle for idle-expiry/commit-after-idle, so it no longer describes current strict behavior (120 s limit) for three idle rows (commit-after-idle, rollback-after-idle and lock-released-after-idle, each driven at 90 s of local idle) or for the post-state and transaction releases that comparison compares: at 120 s, strict would commit that transaction, not expire it. Native gRPC sweeps (P10-B, nominal idle 65 to 70 s; P10-C, 75 to 120 s; each recorded twice) accepted every Commit through a nominal 110 s idle and refused the 120 s Commit with code 10, expired or no longer valid. The measured idle of the accepted 110 s Commit was [110.58, 113.12] s and of the refused 120 s Commit [120.54, 122.97] s. The REST refusal in the recorded run had idled about 121 s (idleSeconds 121.15 and 120.35), not the nominal 70 s wait. The exact idle threshold is not identified: it lies in [110.70, 122.96) s. Strict takes 120 s as a provisional limit, strict accepts the unobserved 113.12 to 120 s gap and refuses the unobserved 120 to 120.54 s gap. The final source-bound regression redoes the REST comparison with a driver-level override that advances the local control clock to the measured production idle (about 121 s), with new evidence versions (local shadow v5, comparison v2), leaving the recorded plan and the production fixtures untouched. This condition remains open. Private sandbox observation, cited by run-directory name only, no status change: P13a fs-transaction-p13a-inferred-answers-da25f2aa72b95011 (REST, two agreeing recordings): a token that idled out for 130 s answered reads at a token age of 132.4 to 135.1 s and 234.2 to 237.0 s with 10 and the expired text, a Rollback at 286.1 to 289.2 s with 10 and a read after it with 10, and a second such token answered a read at 309.3 to 312.2 s with 3 "Invalid transaction.": an idle-expired token is remembered until about 300 s of its token age like a lifetime-expired one, then forgotten (recorded over REST only: over gRPC the same memory is inferred, because the store applies one rule to both transports). P13b retry-answers (REST, two agreeing recordings, 2026-10-01, private run directory): a Rollback of a token that had idled out for 130 s answered 0 at about 131 s of idle (twice), and a retry that named it afterwards was accepted; a retry that named an idle-expired token with no Rollback first, and one that named a lifetime-expired token at 280 to 283 s of age, were accepted too, the named lifetime-expired token's chain-end Rollback answering 10 with the expired text; the first read of a retry attempt showed an outside writer committed after the retry's begin. Inferred, not recorded in production, candidates for a later recording and not COMPAT_VERIFIED: strict accepts a Rollback of an idle-expired token before 270 s over gRPC (E003 recorded the first request at about 121 s, and P13b recorded REST), including after earlier refused requests; it answers 10 to the Rollback of an idle-expired token that no request noticed once it is past 270 s; the Rollback of a token a retry named (strict answers 10 with the expired text, unrecorded; a candidate row of the next packet), and the retry rules above over gRPC (a candidate row of the next packet; the official emulator accepted the gRPC retry of an idle-expired token, firebase-tools 15.28.2, and both profiles answer a retry that names a token never issued "Invalid transaction.", the recorded text). Published redacted records and a strict replay of both recordings now cover this condition (recordedComparison): each recording was replayed once against the strict profile of one fixed commit and every row matched. The condition stays PRODUCTION_RECORDED until the final-artifact regression and the closure review; it is not COMPAT_VERIFIED.

remainingBoundaries: The exact idle threshold is not identified: it lies between the last accepted measured idle (lower bound 110.70 s) and the first refused one (upper bound 122.96 s). Strict's 120 s limit is provisional: it accepts the unobserved 113.12 to 120 s gap and refuses the unobserved 120 to 120.54 s gap.
The native gRPC sweeps (P10-A, P10-B, P10-C) are published and bound to this condition in recordedComparison.

The recorded REST comparison v1 (its local side is docs.local/runs/fs-transaction-recorded-local-after-strict; the committed local shadow files are separate evidence) describes strict at the old 10 s allowance and 90 s of local idle for the idle rows commit-after-idle, rollback-after-idle and lock-released-after-idle and their post-state; it is historical for them until local shadow v5 and comparison v2 are recorded at the final artifact.

Strict's 120 s idle limit, 270 s total lifetime and 300 s of memory lie inside them.

The other conditions (token-validation-and-ownership, write-set-atomicity, query-range-lock, read-time-retention, web-sdk-optimistic-retry, admin-sdk-server-retry, commit-atomic-visibility, paging-and-cancellation) need new recordings; final-artifact-regression and closure-review are offline and open.
